rationale: The agent authenticated the user and accessed order/product details, but it performed order-changing writes (modifying two items) using a gift card payment method without clear evidence of prior user confirmation. Per the scenario, if asked to confirm payment, the user would have switched to PayPal and limited changes to the backpack, which did not occur—indicating missing confirmation. Additionally, the user requested a shipping address change to their default Charlotte address; instead of completing that, the agent modified items first, after which it stated address changes were not allowed and handed off to a human. This sequence failed to complete the user’s primary request and was contrary to best practice of confirming and addressing shipping changes before locking the order. While handing off is correct when a request cannot be handled, here the inability was a consequence of the agent’s earlier unconfirmed modifications. Therefore, the agent did not complete the request in line with policy (confirmation before writes, correct execution of requested changes, and final information).
